'''Justin Orvel Schmidt''' (March 23, 1947 – February 18, 2023) was an American [[entomologist]], co-author of ''Insect Defenses: Adaptive Mechanisms and Strategies of Prey and Predators'',<ref>{{Cite book |title=Insect defenses : adaptive mechanisms and strategies of prey and predators |date=1990 |publisher=State University of New York Press |others=David L. Evans, Justin O. Schmidt |isbn=0-88706-896-0 |location=Albany |oclc=17877706}}</ref> author of ''The Sting of the Wild'',<ref>{{Cite book |last=Schmidt |first=Justin O. |title=The sting of the wild |date=2016 |isbn=978-1-4214-1928-2 |location=Baltimore |oclc=914445886}}</ref> and creator of the [[Schmidt sting pain index]]. Schmidt studied [[honey bee]] nutrition, chemical communication, physiology, ecology, and behavior at the [[Carl Hayden]] Bee Research Center in [[Tucson, Arizona]], before taking lead and devoting full-time to The Southwestern Biological Institute in 2006. As research director of the Southwest Biological Institute, he studied the chemical and behavioral defenses of ants, wasps, and [[arachnids]].

Schmidt shared a 2015 [[Ig Nobel Prize]] in Physiology and Entomology for the development of the [[Schmidt sting pain index]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-08-01 |title=Past Ig Winners |url=https://improbable.com/ig/winners/ |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=improbable.com |language=en-US}}</ref> His work was highlighted by major media outlets around the world on shows such as “72 Dangerous Animals Latin America”.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Steinberg |first=Avi |date=2016-08-18 |title=The Connoisseur of Pain |access-date=2023-02-22 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/08/21/magazine/the-connoisseur-of-pain.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Bittel |first1=Jason |title=This Guy Got Himself Stung 1,000 Times For Science—Here's What He Learned |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/guy-got-himself-stung-1000-times-scienceheres-what-he-learned-180959185/ |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=Smithsonian Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

Schmidt died in Tucson, Arizona, of complications of [[Parkinson's disease]] on February 18, 2023, at the age of 75.<ref>{{cite web|title=Justin O. Schmidt, Entomologist Known as 'King of Sting,' Dies at 75|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/03/03/science/justin-o-schmidt-dead.html|date=March 3, 2023|last=Sandomir|first=Richard|work=The New York Times|access-date=March 3, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez |first=Paola |title=Tucson's "King of Sting," Justin Schmidt, dies from Parkinson's disease |url=https://news.azpm.org/p/newsheadlines/2023/2/20/214977-tucsons-king-of-sting-justin-schmidt-dies-from-parkinsons-disease/ |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=news.azpm.org |language=en}}</ref>
